report.source_text: An MRI of the abdomen taken eight months later reported an interval increase in the size of the left retroperitoneal fat-containing mass, which was now measuring 20 x 18.6 x 22.2 cm and compressing the inferior vena cava (Figure 2). Radiology suggested that although the findings were consistent with the history of a left renal angiomyolipoma, other neoplastic processes such as liposarcoma should be considered in the differential.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old male presented with abdominal distention and pain. Initial CT imaging revealed a large left renal mass (22x13 cm) suspicious for giant renal angiomyolipoma (AML). Eight months later, an MRI showed interval growth of the mass (20x18.6x22.2 cm) and raised suspicion for liposarcoma. The patient underwent a radical left nephrectomy. Gross pathology described a large (39x32x22 cm, 14.36 kg) tan-yellow, lobulated mass. Microscopic pathology (H&E) confirmed well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDL) histologic grade 1, characterized by mature adipocytes and fibrotic stroma with spindle cells, abutting but not invading kidney tissue. The post-operative course was uncomplicated.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with abdominal distention, early satiety, and abdominal/flank pain.
Initial CT scan showed a large (22x13 cm) mixed echogenic lesion adjacent to the left kidney with diffuse fat and soft tissue elements, suspicious for giant renal AML.
Eight months later, MRI showed interval increase in size of the left retroperitoneal fat-containing mass (20x18.6x22.2 cm) and suggested liposarcoma as a differential diagnosis.
The mass was resected via radical left nephrectomy with 2 cm surgical margins.
Gross pathology described a large (39x32x22 cm, 14.36 kg) tan-yellow, lobulated mass that was resected intact.

Microscopic pathology (H&E) showed well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDL) with variably sized mature adipocytes and bands of fibrotic stroma containing spindle cells with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei. The tumor abutted but did not invade adjacent kidney tissue.
The histologic type of the tumor was determined to be a WDL histologic grade 1.
The patient's post-operative course was uncomplicated.
